newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 60,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
Licences are now valid until the end of May but the restitution calculation should continue to be based on the Paris March contract for the time being, they said.
"The market is very flat and it's not a new futures month... May is trading at flat to March anyway," said one trader.
"I think the absolute maximum will be 60,000 tonnes and probably less than 50,000."
The EU awarded 88,250 tonnes in its last tender.

The maximum restitution for licences this week was forecast at a theoretical value of 46.710 Ecus (European Currency Units) per 100 kg of sugar but traders said a level of 46.690 Ecus was The EU restitution was 46.704 Ecus last week.
